cost_leadership.title: Supply chain integration (RHP report)
cost_leadership.body: Backward-integrated, asset-light retail model. Raw material vendors supply gold bullion, silver, diamonds and precious/semi-precious stones, which the Company purchases directly (gold bullion from bullion traders; diamonds mostly from diamond traders and sightholders) on the basis of tax invoices, through purchase orders and without long-term supplier agreements. The Company then supplies raw materials to Karigars (in-house and external) who manufacture jewellery to the Company's designs or designs approved by it, against making charges; the finished jewellery returns to the Company, is hallmarked and quality-checked, and is sold through its own stores - the Company describes itself as 'engaged in the complete value chain of the manufacturing process from designing of jewellery to selling of finished products'. Karigars manufacture more than 79% of products. Two owned/subsidiary Manufacturing Facilities support this: Thirumudivakkam, Chennai (approx. 43,861.96 sq. ft., operations commenced December 2, 2024) run by the Company, and Maraimalainagar, Kanchipuram (approx. 20,000 sq. ft.) run by wholly owned subsidiary Asita Jewellery Manufacturing Private Limited. As of March 31, 2026 the facilities are worked by 816 Karigars on exclusive arrangements and on the rolls of the Company (672 with the Company, 144 with Asita), plus 296 Karigars under short-term non-exclusive agreements. In-house manufacturing is stated to reduce jewellery-making wastage and allow lower value-addition charges to be passed to customers without compromising margins. Old jewellery exchanged or sold back by customers is re-used as raw material, and the Company procures old gold from customers to encourage repeat business. Quality assurance runs two checkpoints before a piece reaches a showroom - an internal quality control department checking purity and finish, then an external government-approved hallmarking centre operating to BIS norms; all loose diamonds are tested by a testing agency and all diamond products certified by an accredited laboratory; finished Karigar output is re-checked for gold, diamond and gemstone quality and design finish. Inventory is bar-coded at all locations and monitored manually and through the 'JILABA ERP' system which carries a built-in inventory management module and gives virtual connectivity across all stores and offices; stock levels are reviewed daily with replenishment action and supply chain is planned season-by-season. Inventory is carried at the lower of net realisable value and cost (annual weighted average cost for gold, silver and diamonds); as at March 31, 2026 gold inventory was Rs 86,830.29 million (Rs 868,302.9 lakhs), silver Rs 8,221.54 million (Rs 82,215.4 lakhs) and diamond and precious/semi-precious stones Rs 3,110.92 million (Rs 31,109.2 lakhs). Total inventory was Rs 98,162.76 million (Rs 981,627.6 lakhs) in FY2026, Rs 58,727.29 million (Rs 587,272.9 lakhs) in FY2025 and Rs 42,920.80 million (Rs 429,208.0 lakhs) in FY2024, with inventory turnover ratio of 2.55, 2.88 and 3.91 times respectively. Downstream, the model is asset-light: of 61 stores only three are owned and the rest are on leave-and-licence; distribution is entirely through own-brand 'Lalithaa' stores supported by in-house sales teams speaking regional languages, a customer-care mobile app, jeweller's block insurance on all goods movement, and insurance coverage at 81.04% of total tangible assets as at March 31, 2026. Working capital is part-funded by customer advances under the jewellery schemes (Rs 50,427.50 million / 20.15% of revenue in FY2026). Employees numbered 7,059 as of March 31, 2026 (senior management 11, managers 430, sales 3,979, security 195, administration 59, back office 1,222, others 1,163), with total attrition of 30.90%, 27.84% and 35.67% in Fiscals 2026, 2025 and 2024 (FY2026 by function: senior management Nil, manager 17.21%, sales 33.83%, security 16.41%, administration 38.98%, back office 35.02%, others 23.90%).

risks.title: Risks (RHP)
risks.body:
- Gold jewellery accounted for 92.33%, 94.58% and 93.96% of revenue from operations in Fiscals 2026, 2025 and 2024. Higher international gold prices, higher import duties, regulatory restrictions, a decline in discretionary spending or a shift in consumer preference would hit almost the entire revenue base.
- The Company does not employ hedging practices such as gold metal loan facilities, forward contracts or options, unlike most of its competitors, so it is directly exposed to gold price fluctuations on both inventory value and demand. Jewellery purchases are discretionary and rising gold prices can cause customers to defer buying.
- The jewellery business requires substantial gold and diamond inventory: inventory was 96.81% of total current assets in Fiscal 2026 and 39.23% of revenue from operations (versus 34.76% in Fiscal 2025 and 25.57% in Fiscal 2024). Working capital rose to Rs 44,661.08 million and working capital days to 65; inventory turnover fell to 2.55x from 2.88x and 3.91x. Delays in inventory turnover or adverse gold/diamond price moves can force write-downs and stretch liquidity.
- The top three suppliers of raw materials contributed 58.03%, 67.20% and 66.98% of total cost of raw materials in Fiscals 2026, 2025 and 2024. Loss of any of these suppliers or interruption in supply of gold bullion would disrupt manufacturing and store replenishment.
- All 61 stores across 51 cities are in Andhra Pradesh, Karnataka, Tamil Nadu, Telangana and Puducherry, with Tamil Nadu alone at 53.98% of Fiscal 2026 revenue. Any regional economic, political, weather or regulatory shock, or region-specific competition, would hit the whole business.
- More than 79% of products are manufactured by Karigars; the Manufacturing Facilities are worked by 816 Karigars on exclusive arrangements plus 296 on non-exclusive short-term agreements as of March 31, 2026. Inability to attract, retain or replace Karigars, or competitors offering them better terms, would disrupt production and add cost.
- Advances from customers were Rs 50,427.50 million in Fiscal 2026 (20.15% of revenue from operations), up from Rs 31,454.10 million (18.61%) and Rs 19,432.26 million (11.58%). This is unsecured customer money funding working capital; any regulatory change to deposit-like schemes, or a fall in enrolments from the 473,412 active customers, would strain liquidity and forward sales visibility.
- The Registered and Corporate Office, 58 of 61 stores as of March 31, 2026, and the Manufacturing Facilities are on leased or leave-and-license premises. Non-renewal, rent escalation or defective title would force relocation of stores whose location is central to footfall and revenue.

commitments.title: Promises (RHP)
commitments.body:
- **Set up 10 New Stores in southern India from the Net Proceeds of the Fresh Issue, all company-operated, in a mix of Large, Medium and Small Format stores.**
- **Open 5 New Stores in Fiscal 2027 out of the 10 New Stores funded by the Net Proceeds.**
- **Open the remaining 5 New Stores in Fiscal 2028 out of the 10 New Stores funded by the Net Proceeds.**
- **Deploy Rs 10,332.31 million (Rs 103,323.10 lakhs) of Net Proceeds towards the 10 New Stores, split as Rs 345.50 million (Rs 3,455.00 lakhs) of fit-out capital expenditure and Rs 9,986.81 million (Rs 99,868.10 lakhs) of inventory cost, …**
- **Any aggregate cost for setting up the New Stores in excess of Rs 10,332.31 million, and all lease-related costs (security deposits and advance rentals), will be funded entirely through internal accruals rather than Offer proceeds.**
- **The amount of Net Proceeds utilised for general corporate purposes shall not exceed 25% of the Gross Proceeds of the Fresh Issue.**
- **Increase focus on studded gold jewellery and other higher-gross-margin gold jewellery categories to lift gross margins, including dedicated display counters in new stores.**
- **Expand the silverware and other lower-value product ranges to mitigate risk from hikes in gold prices (silverware revenue was Rs 16,588.49 million in Fiscal 2026 versus Rs 6,737.08 million in Fiscal 2025).**
- **Continue investing in brand building and marketing initiatives across print, outdoor, digital and below-the-line channels, and continue leveraging the existing customer base through jewellery schemes similar to 'Free-yo-Flexi' and 'Dhana …**
- **Explore opportunities to expand the range of sub-brands and introduce new branded jewellery lines targeted at specific customer niches in gold and studded jewellery.**
- **Expand into 10 identified cities for the New Stores - Chennai (2 stores), Hosur, Kumbakonam, Viluppuram, Dindigul, Cuddalore and Nagapattinam in Tamil Nadu, Hyderabad in Telangana and Belgaum in Karnataka - noting precise locations are not …**
- **Management explicitly flags that the Company does not employ hedging practices such as gold metal loan facilities, forward contracts or options, unlike most competitors, leaving it exposed to major gold price fluctuations.**
